newsitem.title: USA: Staples, Office Depot say deal is off.
newsitem.headline: Staples, Office Depot say deal is off.

text.p: Staples Inc. and Office Depot Inc., after being rebuffed this week by a federal judge, said Wednesday that their $4.6 billion agreement to merge had been terminated.

Following Monday's court ruling, Staples had said it was likely to terminate the deal, which was launched 10 months ago. Staples operates 666 office products superstores worldwide and Office Depot operates 576 stores.
The two companies had acknowledged earlier this week they would likely call off the planned transaction after a federal judge allowed regulators to block the deal.
Originally valued at $4 billion, the deal was worth $4.8 billion based on Wednesday's stock activity.
The companies first announced the deal in September, but the transaction soon ran into trouble when federal and state officials expressed concern it would result in higher prices for office supplies.

On Monday, a federal judge granted a preliminary injunction to the Federal Trade Commission, which had twice turned down the transaction. The injunction permitted the regulators to hold up the deal while the issue made its way through the courts.
The two companies had argued that the combined firm would have less than a 6 percent market share in the fragmented industry.

Wall Street analysts have said Staples is well-positioned to maintain its role as the biggest player in the industry. Office Depot Chief Executive David Fuente told Reuters Tuesday that the company was prepared to resume its expansion.
